newsitem.title: USA: O'Sullivan sees gain from sale of Melnor.
newsitem.headline: O'Sullivan sees gain from sale of Melnor.

text.p: O'Sullivan Corp said Thursday it will sell Melnor Inc to Gardena Holding AG of Ulm, Germany, and recognize a one-time, after-tax divestiture charge of about $0.21 per share in connection with the sale.

The company will record the charge in the third quarter, said O'Sullivan chief financial officer Bryant Nickerson. He said terms of the deal would be disclosed in the company's future financial reports.
Melnor makes lawn and garden watering products. O'Sullivan makes vinyl products for the automotive, medical and office supply industries.
The company said it expects the deal to become effective in August, pending customary conditions including expiration of Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust waiting period.

As a result of the sale, O'Sullivan will have about $28 million to $30 million in cash and no debt. The company said it is currently exploring several small acquisitions, which could result in definitive acquisition agreements in the near future.
